name: Carrie Perrodo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: Ka Yee (Carrie) Wong Perrodo, a native of SIngapore, inherited international oil company Perenco when her husband Hubert Perrodo died in 2006.
Perenco is one of the world's largest family-owned oil companies, with operations in Gabon, Peru, Vietnam and elsewhere.
Carrie's eldest son, Francois, chairs Perenco while her daughter, Nathalie, oversees the family's winery investments in Bordeaux.
forbes_facts: Carrie Perrodo was a top model in the 1970s, when she met Hubert, who was traveling the world in search of oil and gas.
Carrie Perrodo launched her own agency, Carrie's Models. Though she sold it years ago, the agency remains active.

name: Miao Hangen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2006-2026)
forbes_bio: Miao Hangen chairs Eastern Shenghong, a Shenzhen-listed petrochemical and new material firm.
Its parent Shenghong Group, which also has interests in textile and new energy, was founded in 1992.
The group broke ground on a $4.2 billion plant for energy storage system batteries in Zhangjiagang, Jiangsu in July 2023.

name: Huang Xiaolei
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun China (2025-2026); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Huang Xiaolei is the general manager of Eoptolink Technology, a leading supplier of optical modules in China.
Huang cofounded the company with five others, including billionaire Gao Guangrong, in 2008 and took it public in 2016.
Eoptolink gets most of its revenue from overseas markets, reportedly counting Google and Nvidia among its customers.
Eoptolink's Thailand plant, its first overseas production base, came online in 2023. Phase two of the plant started operation in 2025.

name: Alexander Isaev
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Alexander Isaev derives his fortune from Elga, the largest coking coal mine in Russia with about 2.2 billion tonnes of reserves.
In 2021, he and his business partner, Albert Avdolyan, a fellow billionaire who owns the lion's share of Elga, bought coal producer Sibanthracite and later sold it, earning a combined $1 billion.

name: Andrei Kosogov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Andrei Kosogov is a member of Russian conglomerate Alfa Group's supervisory board and is in charge of its investment units.
Kosogov cofounded international investment company LetterOne in 2013. He stepped down from the board in March 2022 after his partners were sanctioned by the EU and the U.K.
LetterOne has invested in oil and gas firm Wintershall Dea, cellular companies Vimpelcom and Turkcell, and health food chain Holland & Barrett.
forbes_facts: Born in Estonia when it was part of the Soviet Union, Kosogov graduated from Moscow Power Engineering Institute.
In 1992, Mikhail Fridman hired Kosogov to oversee the establishment of a privatization investment fund. Months later he became chief executive of Alfa Capital.
